query: How should we select baselines and set failure-injection magnitudes to avoid evaluation overfitting and ensure fair comparisons across architectures?

response.query: How should we select baselines and set failure-injection magnitudes to avoid evaluation overfitting and ensure fair comparisons across architectures?
response.answer: Select baselines from established, well-vetted architectures. Set failure-injection magnitudes based on empirical data to ensure variability and avoid overfitting. Use cross-validation to ensure fair comparisons.

results.content: Our contributions are as follows: • We propose graph convolutional networks (GCNs) (Kipf and Welling, 2017; Chapter 3) for semi-supervised classiﬁcation of nodes in graph-structured data. • We propose graph auto-encoders (GAEs) (Kipf and Welling, 2016; Chap-ter 4) for unsupervised learning and link prediction in graph-structured data. “Nervenet: Learning structured policy with graph neural networks.” In: International Conference on Learning Representations (ICLR). We dragen het volgende bij: • We introduceren graph convolutional networks (GCNs) (Kipf and Welling, 2017; Hoofdstuk 3) voor semi-supervised classiﬁcatie van knopen in graaf gestructureerde data. • We introduceren graph auto-encoders (GAEs) (Kipf and Welling, 2016; Hoofdstuk 4) voor unsupervised learning en het voorspellen van zijden in graaf gestructureerde data.
